brief.headline: The one-day contango did not survive: the 06-Aug official settled cash $3,261.00 (+$32.00, +0.99%) against a 3M of $3,260.00, restoring a token $1.00 backwardation and taking flat price to a six-week high - because the Hormuz routing announcement that knocked $42.00 off the prompt on Wednesday produced no measurable change in transit counts, no restarted capacity, and no interruption to a 27th consecutive warehouse draw to 257,900 t.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. Cash $3,261.00, up $32.00 (+0.99%) from $3,229.00 and the highest official settlement since 23-June; 3M $3,260.00, up $30.50 (+0.94%); stock 257,900 t, down another 1,500 t for a 27th consecutive draw and a fresh cycle low, now 49.4% below where 2026 opened. Note the SHAPE: Wednesday was a prompt-only collapse (cash -$42.00 against 3M -$7.00); Thursday was a near-parallel recovery (+$32.00 against +$30.50). The cash-3M structure therefore only crept from a $0.50 contango back to a $1.00 backwardation - it recovered $1.50 of the $35.00 it lost.

WHY IT MOVED. Nothing in the diplomacy reversed. Iran and Oman still have an agreed set of geographical coordinates for a proposed commercial routing, the joint statement is still described as in final review and drafting, and Tehran still states explicitly that the arrangement does not restore safe navigation. What did not arrive was CONFIRMATION IN THE PHYSICAL DATA. Published transit counts stayed in single digits - eight vessels on Monday 03-Aug against roughly 130 a day before hostilities began on 28-February - while war-risk cover for Gulf transits remains quoted at 3-10% of hull value against about 0.25% pre-war. Announcements move the prompt; throughput moves the deficit, and throughput has not moved.

WHAT THE TWO SESSIONS TOGETHER ACTUALLY PROVE. Read as a pair, 05-Aug and 06-Aug are the cleanest natural experiment of the year for separating the two components of this rally. The CORRIDOR-RISK component sits almost entirely in the prompt, is worth roughly $35/t of cash-3M structure, and proved instantly reversible on a headline. The STRUCTURAL component sits in the whole curve - a policy-capped Chinese supply base at its 45 Mt ceiling, outside-China output down 6.7% year-on-year in July, exchange stock at a century low - and did not move on either day. The flat-price recovery to a six-week high says the market re-rated the second component once the first failed to deliver.

WHAT TO WATCH. Three observables, in order of information value. First, whether the 27-session stock draw finally breaks - a BUILD would be far more significant than any further draw, and none has appeared through either the collapse or the rebound. Second, whether the Iran-Oman joint statement is actually signed and, more importantly, whether published transit counts start recovering toward pre-war levels; the announcement has already been paid for, the throughput has not. Third, whether the cash-3M spread can rebuild past a token $1.00 while stock makes new lows - a curve that cannot re-establish a meaningful backwardation against a century-low warehouse is telling you the front-month scarcity was a corridor artefact rather than a warehouse one.

kpis.label: LME Cash settlement
kpis.note: 06-Aug OFFICIAL $3,261.00 versus 05-Aug $3,229.00 = +$32.00 (+0.99%), recovering the whole of Wednesday's $42.00 Hormuz-headline give-back bar $10.00 and setting the highest official cash settlement since 23-June. The rebound came WITHOUT a reversal in the diplomacy: the Iran-Oman routing agreement announced 05-Aug still stands, the joint statement is still in drafting, and Tehran still says navigation is not restored. What changed is that the physical evidence refused to confirm the headline - published transit counts stayed at single digits against roughly 130 vessels a day before the war, and exchange stock drew a 27th consecutive session to 257,900 t. avg = JULY-2026 monthly mean $3,155.98 (final, Westmetall averages page); the August month-to-date mean now stands at $3,255.25 over four sessions. SOURCING AND AN IMPORTANT METHOD NOTE FOR THIS RUN. At this ~06:00-London compile Westmetall had NOT yet published the 06-Aug LME board on either the English or the German overview, and both per-metal daily tables still ended at 05-Aug - the fifth cache/lag failure of this source inside a fortnight, and the first time the lag hit BOTH language versions and BOTH the overview and the daily tables simultaneously. The 06-Aug session was nevertheless already inside Westmetall's own PUBLISHED August month-to-date averages pages, which had rolled from three sessions to four. The 06-Aug officials below are therefore RECOVERED ARITHMETICALLY from two published Westmetall figures - the August month-to-date mean and the 03/04/05-Aug daily table - and are not estimates: for every metal the back-solve resolves to a UNIQUE value inside LME's 0.50 tick (aluminium cash 3,255.25 x 4 = 13,021.00 less 9,760.00 = 3,261.00 exactly), and each recovered stock lands on LME's 25 t reporting increment (6 t for nickel). Two independent cross-checks agree: Westmetall's own 06-Aug German copper notations jumped about 2.0% on the day, consistent with the recovered copper cash of $14,455.00, and Trading Economics' separate 06-Aug marks (aluminium 3,261.95, zinc 3,793.35, lead 1,898.03, nickel 16,735.38 - a different CFD basis) match the recovered board in direction and level on every metal. The whole board sits on ONE uniform session, 06-Aug-2026.

On 05-Aug cash fell $42.00 while the 3M fell only $7.00: the market unwound a PROMPT risk premium and left the forward alone. kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: BACK INTO BACKWARDATION, BUT ONLY JUST: cash $3,261.00 against 3M $3,260.00 = a $1.00 BACKWARDATION, against a $0.50 CONTANGO on 05-Aug and a +$34.50 backwardation on 04-Aug. CONVENTION: cash above 3M is BACKWARDATION; cash below 3M is CONTANGO. The one-day contango did not survive a single session, which argues 05-Aug was a risk unwind rather than a regime change - but the structure has NOT gone back to where it was. A $1.00 prompt premium is functionally flat and is $33.50 narrower than Tuesday's. NOTE THE DIVERGENCE, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE SIGN TO WEDNESDAY'S: on 05-Aug the spread and the flat price fell TOGETHER; on 06-Aug the flat price rose $30.50 while the spread widened only $1.50. Price is recovering faster than structure. avg = July-2026 mean cash-3M spread of $7.05 (Westmetall July means: cash $3,155.98 less 3M $3,148.93).

lme.commentary: THE SESSION IN ONE LINE: the announcement was sold on Wednesday and the absence of follow-through was bought on Thursday. Cash rose $32.00 (+0.99%) to $3,261.00 and the 3-month rose $30.50 (+0.94%) to $3,260.00, restoring a $1.00 BACKWARDATION after a single session of $0.50 contango, and taking both legs to their highest since late June. THE SHAPE IS THE SIGNAL. Wednesday's move was almost entirely prompt: cash -$42.00 against a 3M -$7.00, which unwound roughly $35.00 of cash-3M structure on the Iran-Oman routing announcement. Thursday's move was almost perfectly parallel: +$32.00 against +$30.50, which shifted the whole curve and returned only $1.50 of that structure. A parallel shift is not a prompt squeeze; it is the market re-rating the durability of the deficit rather than the immediacy of it. THE FACT THAT NEVER BLINKED: exchange stock drew 1,500 t to 257,900 t, a 27th consecutive session and a fresh cycle low, -49.4% year-to-date. The warehouse drew through the collapse and drew through the rebound; it has not acknowledged the diplomatic development at any point. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE READ: a first stock BUILD, or a cash-3M spread that fails to rebuild past a token dollar over several sessions, would say the tightness regime is genuinely ending. A backwardation that widens back toward $30-40 while stock keeps drawing would say Wednesday was a one-day risk unwind and nothing more. On one session of evidence the second reading is ahead, but only just.

drivers.text: THE HORMUZ ROUTING ANNOUNCEMENT DID NOT CONVERT INTO THROUGHPUT, AND THE PROMPT PREMIUM CAME BACK - FROM A $0.50 CONTANGO ON 05-AUG TO A $1.00 BACKWARDATION ON 06-AUG — The diplomacy itself has not reversed: Iran and Oman have agreed the geographical coordinates of a proposed commercial routing and the joint statement remains in final review and drafting. The reported shape of the deal is a northern inbound lane through Iranian waters and a southern outbound lane in Omani waters, initially for 60 days with no transit fees, with mine-clearing in the centre of the strait still under discussion. WHAT HAS NOT HAPPENED IS THE OBSERVABLE. Published transit counts remained in single digits - eight vessels on Monday 03-Aug - against roughly 130 ships a day before hostilities began on 28-February. Iran has stated that reopening is contingent on the US removing its naval blockade, and US sanctions may themselves prevent shipping companies from coordinating with Iranian authorities absent an explicit exemption. Every regional premium row carries a Gulf-risk component; the LME curve wrote that component to zero on Wednesday and wrote about $1.50 of it back on Thursday, which is the market's own estimate that the announcement is real but not yet operative.
drivers.source: Al Jazeera - Iran, Oman, US close to Hormuz deal: what do they all want (05-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: THE US TARIFF LEG IS $1,630.50/t AND ROSE $16.00 THIS SESSION FOR PURELY ARITHMETIC REASONS - SECTION 232 IS VERIFIED AT 50% ON ALUMINIUM ARTICLES — Verified this run against US Customs and Border Protection guidance CSMS #68855869 (05-Jun-2026) implementing Proclamation 11032, effective 08-Jun-2026. Aluminium articles under HTSUS 9903.82.02 carry 50% on the FULL customs value - the metal/non-metal content split was eliminated by the 06-Apr-2026 proclamation. Predominantly-metal derivatives under Annex I-B carry 25%; the newly added Annex I-C list of mobile industrial equipment carries 25% through 31-Dec-2027; US-smelt-and-cast content is 10%; the UK rate is 25% on articles and 15% on derivatives; Russia remains at 200% and stacks outside this scheme. The US-content threshold was relaxed from 95% to 85% effective 08-Jun-2026. NO SECTION 232 ALUMINIUM ANNOUNCEMENT WAS FOUND DATED 05-07 AUGUST 2026. THE MECHANICAL POINT FOR PREMIUM READERS: at 50% ad valorem the tariff component of a US delivered price is 50% of LME cash, so it rose $16.00/t on 06-Aug purely because cash rose $32.00 - no change in physical tightness is implied by that increase. CAUTION FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED: the 15% carve-out at HTSUS 9903.82.22 covering Argentina, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Japan, Korea, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, Taiwan, the UK and EU member states is described in the CBP text as applying to derivative STEEL articles; it should be checked against US note 16(c)(xi) before being applied on the aluminium side, and this board does not apply it.
drivers.source: US Customs and Border Protection - CSMS #68855869, Section 232 guidance effective 08-Jun-2026

drivers.text: FREIGHT IS ADDING TO DELIVERED PREMIUMS INDEPENDENTLY OF THE GULF - BALTIC DRY AT 3,063, +53.6% YEAR-ON-YEAR AND A FIFTH CONSECUTIVE GAIN — The Baltic Dry Index rose 4.33% to 3,063 points on Wednesday 05-Aug, its fifth straight gain and the highest since 03-June, with Capesize +6.6% to 5,094 and Panamax +2.2% to 2,236. The index is +9.5% over the month and +53.6% year-on-year. Part of the early-August move is attributed to Typhoon Dolphin rather than to Gulf disruption, which is precisely why it matters for premium readers: it is a freight cost increase that a Hormuz reopening would NOT reverse. Gulf war-risk cover is a separate and much larger line, still quoted at 3-10% of hull value against roughly 0.25% before hostilities, which on a $100m vessel is $3-10m per transit against about $250,000 pre-war. NO PUBLISHED BDI PRINT FOR 06 OR 07 AUGUST WAS FOUND; the 05-Aug level is carried and dated.

THE PHYSICAL PREMIUM COMPLEX IS THE WEAKEST-SOURCED PART OF THIS BOARD AND THAT IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER — Every spot premium row here - CIF Japan, EDU Rotterdam, Rotterdam billets, US Midwest transaction and US Midwest duty-paid - is carried at an assessment date of 03-Jul-2026 or earlier, because Platts, Fastmarkets and Argus publish these assessments only to subscribers. A dedicated public search this run returned NO regional premium assessment dated in August 2026. The ONLY premium figures on this board that are both current and independently verifiable are the MJP QUARTERLY SETTLEMENT of $395/t for Q3-2026, which is public in two independent sources, and the TARIFF DECOMPOSITION, which is computed from a verified statutory rate and the day's LME official. One genuinely new public reference point did appear: Fastmarkets first published its CIF Rotterdam aluminium billet premium calculated assessment on 31-Jul-2026. This board does not fabricate freight, financing or tightness splits for premium rows, and does not present stale marks as live ones.

SMM's most recent free alumina commentary continues to describe a market in the doldrums with cost support wrestling weak demand, port inventory building on high overseas arrivals and the oversupply pattern unchanged, and SMM's stated precondition for any bullish driver - implementation of Guinea's bauxite quota policy - has still not been met. Against that, the 05-Aug transaction of 30,000 mt at $356/mt FOB East Australia for September loading is a firm ex-China print that does not fit the doldrums framing. SMM puts the Chinese industry average full cost near 2,530 yuan/mt on Guinea bauxite at $70-75/mt, so the Chinese contract remains only a few per cent above its cost floor while the seaborne market is transacting higher. Watch whether that gap pulls Chinese prices up or seaborne prices back.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THE ANNOUNCEMENT STANDS; THE THROUGHPUT HAS NOT MOVED, AND THAT GAP IS WHY THE LME PROMPT PREMIUM CAME BACK ON 06-AUG. Iran and Oman have agreed the geographical coordinates of a proposed commercial shipping route and the joint statement remains in final review and drafting. The reported structure of the deal: inbound vessels would use a NORTHERN lane through Iranian waters and outbound vessels a SOUTHERN lane in Omani waters coordinated with Iran, initially for 60 DAYS WITH NO TRANSIT FEES, with clearing of naval mines from the centre of the strait still under discussion. Iran has already dropped its demand for control of both directions. THE OBSTACLES ARE SPECIFIC AND UNRESOLVED: Iran states that reopening is contingent on the US removing its naval blockade and halting attacks on Iranian infrastructure; it is unsettled who administers the waterway longer term and whether Iran may eventually levy maritime service fees; and US sanctions may themselves prevent shipping companies from coordinating with Iranian authorities absent an explicit exemption. THE OBSERVABLE REMAINS FLAT ON THE FLOOR: eight vessels transited on Monday 03-Aug against roughly 130 ships a day before the war began on 28-February. UKMTO reported a cargo ship struck by an unidentified projectile off Oman on Tuesday 04-Aug. The trend flag is moved from DOWN back to FLAT this run: the diplomatic direction remains improved, but a week of headlines has produced no measurable change in throughput and the corridor still operates at a small fraction of normal commercial volume.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: NO NEW PUBLIC COUNT SINCE 31-JUL AT THIS REFRESH - the figure is carried, not marked to today. Bab al Mandeb carried 31 commodity vessels on Friday 31-Jul, up from 29 a day earlier, but only after collapsing to a weekly low of 16 on 26-Jul following the Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping declared on 20-Jul. The Houthis claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, prompting Saudi Arabia to divert crude exports to the Suez routing. With both Gulf chokepoints impaired simultaneously, the freight and insurance wedge compounds on Gulf-origin metal and on Suez-routed alumina and semis alike. UPDATE 06-AUG: the Red Sea leg is NOT following Hormuz. Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen claimed on 05-Aug that they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, and a ship was reported hit in the Red Sea on the same day. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address the Bab al Mandeb constraint, so the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes remains impaired and the two chokepoints are now diverging for the first time since the escalation.

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: UNCHANGED AND STILL THE CLEANEST PRICE-BASED REFUTATION OF THE REOPENING NARRATIVE. War-risk cover for Gulf transits is quoted at 3-10% of hull value, with more recent quotes cited at 7.5-10%, against roughly 0.25% before hostilities began. In cash terms a $100m vessel faces $3-10m per transit against about $250,000 pre-war; pre-conflict single-transit and one-week additional war-risk premiums ran 0.15-0.25% of insured hull value. Lloyd's List describes Gulf war-risk premiums as topping double-digit millions of dollars per trip, and some insurers have withdrawn cover entirely. WHY THIS ROW IS THE ONE TO WATCH RATHER THAN THE HEADLINES: insurers price realised risk with their own capital and have no incentive to anticipate a diplomatic outcome. Underwriters had a full session to react to the Iran-Oman coordinates agreement and did not reprice. A sustained fall in this line - not a signed statement - is what would confirm the corridor is genuinely reopening, and it would show up in delivered premiums well before it shows up in exchange stock.

THE PRACTICAL POINT FOR CONTRACTING: the 48-hour swing from claimed deal perimeters to a public accusation of duplicity and a fresh vessel strike is exactly the volatility that keeps force-majeure and war-risk language live in Gulf-origin contracts, regardless of which way the next headline points.

THE ALUMINIUM READ, WHICH RUNS IN TWO DIRECTIONS: energy is 30-40% of smelter cash cost and petroleum coke feeds the prebaked anode, so a cheaper crude complex lowers the industry cost floor and will price into the mid-August anode, CTP and green-petcoke settlement cycle. headlines.title: THE ONE-SESSION CONTANGO REVERSED: the 06-Aug official settled cash $3,261.00 (+$32.00, +0.99%) against a 3M of $3,260.00 (+$30.50, +0.94%), restoring a $1.00 BACKWARDATION and taking both legs to six-week highs. The shape matters more than the size - Wednesday was a prompt-only collapse (cash -$42.00 against 3M -$7.00) while Thursday was a near-parallel shift, so only $1.50 of the $35.00 of lost prompt structure came back. That is a market re-rating the durability of the deficit, not re-squeezing the front month.

EXCHANGE STOCK DREW A 27TH CONSECUTIVE SESSION to 257,900 t, down another 1,500 t and a fresh cycle low, now 49.4% below the 509,250 t that opened 2026. THIS IS THE FACT THAT NEVER BLINKED: the warehouse drew through Wednesday's prompt collapse and drew again through Thursday's rebound, and has not acknowledged the Hormuz diplomacy at any point. LME aluminium stocks are at their lowest level this century, with Russian-origin metal making up the bulk of what remains - metal that is LME-deliverable but that many consumers will not take.

THE IRAN-OMAN HORMUZ ROUTING AGREEMENT STANDS BUT HAS NOT CONVERTED. Coordinates are agreed and the joint statement remains in final review and drafting; the reported structure is a northern inbound lane in Iranian waters and a southern outbound lane in Omani waters, initially for 60 days with no transit fees, with mine-clearing still under discussion. Iran states reopening is contingent on the US lifting its naval blockade, and US sanctions may prevent shippers coordinating with Iranian authorities absent an exemption. Eight vessels transited on 03-Aug against roughly 130 a day pre-war.

CHINA HAS EFFECTIVELY REACHED ITS 45 Mt CAPACITY CEILING and the pricing logic is visibly shifting. 2025 primary output was 45.02 Mt against the self-imposed cap, H1-2026 output was 22.34 Mt, and industry commentary describes room for further expansion as effectively exhausted - the sector has exited the era of volume-driven growth. Domestic pricing is rotating to regional flows, lifting the South China premium by RMB 60-100/t on a southwest conversion surge. China's net aluminium exports are down roughly 700,000 t year-to-date, keeping ex-China markets structurally tight.

OUTPUT OUTSIDE CHINA FELL 6.7% YEAR-ON-YEAR IN JULY, principally on reduced operating rates at Middle Eastern smelters. Alba's Q2 net finished production was 155,469 t, DOWN 61% year-on-year, with Lines 1, 2 and 3 still under controlled shutdown; EGA must restore all 1,262 reduction cells at Al Taweelah and had restarted 89 as of its 02-July disclosure, with full recovery guided at up to a year. Alba's own market read put the Q2 global deficit at 934,000 t including China and 626,000 t excluding China.

CENTURY ALUMINUM BEAT ON Q2 AND GUIDED HIGHER: adjusted EBITDA $326.9m against $315-335m guidance and $231.4m in Q1, on shipments of 130,632 t and net sales of $752.1m; adjusted EPS $2.46. Q3 guidance $325-345m. The purest US and Section-232 read in the peer set, with the last 90 Mt. Holly pots restarted and cash exceeding total debt as of end-July. Management flagged unfavourable raw-material price realisation as the main EBITDA headwind - the same cost-side signal the input basket shows.

THE RESTART PIPELINE IS DATED AND REAL, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST BEARISH ARGUMENT AVAILABLE. Slovalco will restart 75,000 t of the 175,000 t curtailed at its Slovak smelter with production targeted in Q4-2026, backed by a EUR 100m investment and a long-term state-utility power contract plus EU ETS indirect-cost compensation. Magnitude 7 Metals is restarting potline one at New Madrid, Missouri (about 75,000 t/y) before year-end, explicitly citing the 50% Section 232 tariff. Century's Mt. Holly expansion is complete. EGA continues restoring Al Taweelah.

Seaborne alumina transacted at $356/mt FOB East Australia on 05-Aug. Against that, Brent near $79-80 and TTF near EUR 53.67/MWh lower the far larger energy leg.

Alcoa agreed to acquire South32's aluminium value-chain assets - Worsley Alumina, Hillside, MRN bauxite and the Brazilian alumina and aluminium interests - for up to US$5.6bn, with Mozal excluded and remaining on care and maintenance. The framework in force since 08-June applies the duty to the FULL customs value with no metal content split, 25% on predominantly-metal derivatives and on the new Annex I-C mobile-equipment list through 31-Dec-2027, 10% on US smelt-and-cast content, 25% for the UK and 200% for Russia; the US-content threshold was relaxed from 95% to 85%. Separately India raised its aluminium import levy to 8.25%, lifting MSME raw-material costs despite a domestic surplus.

trade.note: Indicative corridors with publicly sourced shares/figures - NOT tonnage estimates. Normally refreshed monthly; REFRESHED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE, because the Hormuz regime produced its first concrete diplomatic output. On 05-Aug Iran's Foreign Ministry confirmed that Tehran and Muscat had agreed the geographical coordinates of a proposed commercial shipping route through the strait, with a joint statement in final review and drafting; Iran's deputy foreign minister said BOTH existing lanes would close in favour of a new transit model, TEMPORARY and expected to be usable for two to four months, and Tehran stated explicitly that this does not mean safe navigation is restored. THE GULF CORRIDOR IS NOT RE-CLASSIFIED, and that is deliberate and evidence-based: the published transit count did not move. Kpler recorded eight vessels through the strait on 05-Aug and 106 crossings by 96 distinct vessels over 27-Jul to 02-Aug, about 15 a day against roughly 130-140 before 28-February. Transit counts, not communiques, are the observable that would justify moving a corridor from 'tightening' to 'easing'. SEPARATELY, THE TWO CHOKEPOINTS HAVE DIVERGED: Houthi forces claimed on 05-Aug to have targeted a Saudi tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further Red Sea vessels, so the Bab al Mandeb leg is not following Hormuz.

flows.note: About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf metal is exported; Gulf output was -34.5% y/y in June and outside-China output was -6.7% y/y in July. Transit has been the binding constraint rather than production - but production is also impaired in its own right: EGA at 89 of 1,262 pots on 02-Jul and Alba's Lines 1-3 (19% of 1,623,000 t/y) shut since 15-Mar and confirmed still shut in its 04-Aug Q2 disclosure. THE 05-AUG IRAN-OMAN AGREEMENT ON ROUTE COORDINATES IS THE FIRST CONCRETE STEP TOWARD A REOPENING, and it is deliberately NOT treated as one here: the route is temporary (two to four months by Iran's own account), both existing lanes would close in its favour, Tehran says safe navigation is not restored, and the published count on the day was eight vessels against roughly 130-140 pre-war. Kept at 'tightening' pending observable transit recovery. Even a full transit reopening leaves the production impairment in place for quarters.

flows.note: THE RED SEA IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ. catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL, 13:20 London. Three reads, in order of information value: (1) does the cash-3M backwardation rebuild past a token $1.00, which is the test of whether Wednesday was a one-day risk unwind or the start of a flat structure; (2) does exchange stock post its FIRST BUILD in 28 sessions, which would be far more significant than any further draw; (3) does the 3M hold above the $3,229.50 short-term invalidation, now $30.50 below the 06-Aug close.

HINDALCO Q1 FY27 RESULTS, board meeting today with the call at 16:00 IST. The downstream leg is already known and strong - Novelis reported net income of $164m (+71%), adjusted EBITDA $516m (+24%) at $563/t on the Oswego restart and Bay Minette commissioning. The open question is UPSTREAM, where management has guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation and the India Aluminium Upstream EBITDA strip has risen four consecutive quarters to a record RS 5,448cr in Q4 FY26. A fifth consecutive rise would corroborate the peer-set message; a break would corroborate Century's raw-material warning.

WHETHER THE IRAN-OMAN JOINT STATEMENT IS SIGNED - AND, FAR MORE IMPORTANTLY, WHETHER PUBLISHED TRANSIT COUNTS RECOVER. The announcement has already been paid for and partially unwound; the throughput has not moved. Eight vessels transited on 03-Aug against roughly 130 a day pre-war. Unresolved obstacles are specific: Iran ties reopening to removal of the US naval blockade, mine-clearing in the centre of the strait is still under discussion, and US sanctions may prevent shippers coordinating with Iranian authorities absent an exemption.

WHETHER THE 27-SESSION STOCK DRAW ENDS. Exchange stock is 257,900 t, a fresh cycle low and -49.4% year-to-date, falling at an almost mechanical 1,500-1,750 t per session since mid-July. The first BUILD would be far more informative than any further draw: metal returning to warehouse alongside a flat or negative prompt spread would be the clearest confirmation available that the tightness regime has ended. The warehouse has drawn through both the collapse and the rebound without deviating.

GULF WAR-RISK INSURANCE QUOTES - the cleanest price-based test available, because underwriters price realised risk with their own capital and have no incentive to anticipate a diplomatic outcome. Cover is still quoted at 3-10% of hull value, with recent quotes cited at 7.5-10%, against roughly 0.25% pre-war; some insurers have withdrawn entirely. A sustained fall below about 2% would confirm a genuine reopening well before it showed up in exchange stock, and would flow into delivered premiums first.

SMM WEEKLY CHINA ALUMINIUM INGOT AND BILLET SOCIAL INVENTORY - the direct test of whether Chinese destocking holds through the high-temperature off-season. SMM has attributed recent destocking to a rising liquid-aluminium share and supply contraction rather than to demand pull, and flags weak traditional end-use demand with cast alloy operating rates falling and orders shrinking. With China now at its 45 Mt policy ceiling and net exports down about 700,000 t year-to-date, Chinese inventory increasingly signals domestic premium direction rather than LME direction.

THE PREBAKED ANODE, COAL TAR PITCH AND GREEN PETCOKE SETTLEMENT CYCLE, priced around the 17th-18th - the single most informative input event of the month and the first hard evidence of whether the early-August energy fall feeds the carbon leg. Petcoke is about 70% of prebaked anode cost, and the August cycle prices against a crude complex that fell roughly 5% in each of two sessions to a three-week low. July's anode benchmark was RMB 5,683/t cash, up RMB 30 month-on-month, which snapped the prior downtrend with margins hovering just above breakeven.

WHETHER THE ALUMINA AND BAUXITE FIRMING IS CONFIRMED OR ISOLATED. A single 05-Aug transaction of 30,000 mt at $356/mt FOB East Australia sits $52/t above the last publicly verifiable Platts reference, and no second seaborne trade has printed publicly since. Underneath it SMM's imported bauxite index rose to $71.57/mt on 06-Aug with AUGUST GUINEA LONG-TERM CONTRACTS STILL UNSETTLED and rumoured higher - that settlement is the next scheduled hard datapoint. Watch also for any move on Guinea's export-quota policy, which SMM identifies as the swing factor.

Q4-2026 MJP CIF JAPAN PREMIUM NEGOTIATIONS expected to open, off an 11-year-high Q3 settlement of $395/t. The backdrop swung back toward SELLERS this run: the prompt contango lasted one session and the physical case for a softer settlement did not materialise. Buyers retain a firmer yen near 157.9 after the first joint US-Japan intervention since 2011. Sellers hold exchange stock at 257,900 t, Alba's three shut potlines and EGA's pot count. Scenario range carried here: $320-415, a construct rather than an assessment.

CHALCO H1-2026 INTERIM RESULTS, expected around late August - the largest single gap in the peer set. Chalco reported Q1-2026 net profit attributable of RMB 5.527bn, +56.35% year-on-year, and FY2025 of RMB 12.674bn. It publishes no EBITDA line in any period. Then CHINA AUGUST PMIs AND INDUSTRIAL OUTPUT, testing whether July's split between the private RatingDog gauge at 50.9 and official NBS at 49.2 resolves upward or downward, and the 15-16 SEPTEMBER FOMC WITH DOTS, where the early-August fall in crude and European gas has materially improved the disinflation arithmetic.

risks.text: THE DIPLOMATIC TRIGGER FIRED AND FAILED TO CONVERT, WHICH LOWERS THE NEAR-TERM RISK WITHOUT REMOVING IT. Iran and Oman have agreed the coordinates of a proposed Hormuz routing and the joint statement remains in final review and drafting, but one full week on there has been no measurable change in any physical observable: transit counts stayed in single digits against roughly 130 vessels a day pre-war, war-risk cover stayed at 3-10% of hull value, and no curtailed Gulf capacity restarted. The LME curve gave up $35/t of prompt structure on the announcement and took $1.50 of it back the next session. The June precedent remains on the official record - on the 17-June ceasefire official cash fell from $3,855.00 to $3,061.50, -20.6% - and a signed statement with a start date is available at any time. What limits it is that the route is temporary by Tehran's own account and reopening is tied to removal of the US naval blockade.

THE PROMPT PREMIUM HAS NOT REBUILT AND THAT IS THE MOST UNDER-DISCUSSED RISK ON THIS BOARD. The cash-3M structure went +$48.00 on 03-Aug, +$34.50 on 04-Aug, a $0.50 CONTANGO on 05-Aug and only +$1.00 on 06-Aug. The contango did not survive a session, which argues against a regime change - but a $1.00 backwardation against a warehouse at its lowest level this century is functionally flat, and it is the clearest evidence available that consumers are not currently bidding for immediate metal. THE RISK IS THAT FLAT PRICE IS RUNNING AHEAD OF STRUCTURE: cash made a six-week high on 06-Aug while the spread added $1.50. If the backwardation cannot rebuild past $20-30 over the coming sessions while stock continues to draw, the honest conclusion is that front-month scarcity was a corridor artefact and the flat-price recovery is borrowing against a forward deficit that is already well priced.

SUPPLY IS RETURNING ON A DATED AND FUNDED SCHEDULE AND THIS IS THE STRONGEST BEARISH ARGUMENT THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON GEOPOLITICS AT ALL. Slovalco will restart 75,000 t with production targeted in Q4-2026, backed by a EUR 100m investment, a long-term state-utility power contract and EU ETS indirect-cost compensation. Magnitude 7 Metals is restarting about 75,000 t at New Madrid before year-end, explicitly citing the 50% Section 232 tariff. Century's Mt. Holly expansion is complete, taking the plant to full capacity for the first time since 2015, and Grundartangi Line 2 is near full. Alcoa's Portland restart lifted shipments 18% to 726,000 t. EGA continues restoring Al Taweelah. Outside-China daily-average output rose month-on-month in July even as the year-on-year comparison fell 6.7%, and the falling energy cost floor makes the European leg of this pipeline materially cheaper to execute.

THE COST FLOOR HAS SPLIT, AND THE SIDE THAT IS RISING IS ALREADY VISIBLE IN PRODUCER P&Ls. Energy fell - Brent near $79-80 after roughly 5% declines in each of two sessions, TTF near EUR 53.67/MWh - which lowers the industry cost floor and removes the mechanism that would force supply discipline on a falling price. Against that the raw-material leg is firming: SMM's imported bauxite index rose to $71.57/mt on 06-Aug, +$0.70 w/w, with Guinea sellers at $72-73 against refinery bids of $70-71, August long-term contracts unsettled and rumoured higher, and freight to China up to about $35/mt; 30,000 mt of alumina transacted at $356/mt FOB East Australia on 05-Aug. THE CORROBORATION IS INDEPENDENT AND IT IS NOW REPEATED: Century cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for a second consecutive quarter. A rising LME is not converting one-for-one into margin.

CHINESE DOWNSTREAM DEMAND REMAINS THE WEAK LINK, ALTHOUGH THE POLICY CEILING IS NOW DOING MORE WORK THAN DEMAND ON THE PRICE. The official NBS manufacturing PMI is in contraction at 49.2 against the private RatingDog gauge at 50.9, and the high-temperature off-season is cutting cast alloy operating rates and orders. What has changed is the supply side of the same market: China has effectively reached its 45 Mt policy ceiling, with 2025 output at 45.02 Mt and H1-2026 at 22.34 Mt, and industry commentary describes room for expansion as exhausted. Domestic pricing is rotating to regional flows, lifting the South China premium by RMB 60-100/t on a southwest conversion surge, and net exports are down roughly 700,000 t year-to-date. Weak Chinese demand now depresses Chinese premiums more than it depresses the LME, because the metal is not leaving in the volumes it used to.

THE Q4 MJP PREMIUM NEGOTIATION SWUNG BACK TOWARD SELLERS THIS RUN AFTER SWINGING TO BUYERS LAST RUN, AND THE SWING IS AGAIN CURVE-BASED. The prompt contango that opened the buyers' argument on 05-Aug lasted exactly one session; the 06-Aug official restored a $1.00 backwardation with cash at a six-week high. More decisively, the physical confirmation the buyers needed did not arrive - transit counts flat, war-risk cover unchanged, no Gulf restarts. Sellers hold the harder facts: exchange stock at 257,900 t after 27 draws, Alba's Lines 1-3 still shut with Q2 output -61% year-on-year, EGA at 89 of 1,262 pots. Buyers retain a firmer yen near 157.9 after the first joint US-Japan intervention since 2011. Talks are expected to open around late August off an 11-year-high $395/t Q3 settlement; the scenario range carried here is narrowed to $320-415 and is a construct, not an assessment.

THE BASE COMPLEX IS CONFIRMING RATHER THAN CONTRADICTING THE ALUMINIUM MOVE, WHICH IS A RISK TO THE BEARISH CASE. On the 06-Aug board copper made a fresh 2026 high at $14,455.00 cash, up $287.50 (+2.03%), with its exchange stock drawing a further 5,175 t to 226,650 t; zinc added $120.00 to $3,857.00 on a 975 t draw; lead added $6.00. Only nickel fell, by $320.00. Copper also did NOT follow aluminium's prompt collapse on 05-Aug. A broadly firm industrial-metals tape with copper at new highs on heavy stock draws is direct evidence that Thursday's aluminium rebound was not an isolated geopolitical retracement but part of a wider industrial bid. External demand data support this: the private RatingDog July manufacturing PMI printed 50.9 with new orders up a 14th consecutive month, and Korea 53.1, Taiwan 55.1 and Vietnam 52.9 all expanded.

MONETARY POLICY RISK IS BROADLY UNCHANGED AND MODESTLY IMPROVED BY THE ENERGY FALL. The dollar index edged back to about 99.80, +0.12%, still below the round number it briefly cleared on Tuesday, and the LME EUR/USD fixing eased to 1.15460 from 1.15530. The Fed held 9-3 on 29-July with three dissents FOR a hike; Governor Cook said this week she would support hikes if disinflation does not resume while also allowing that inflation may ease enough to avoid them. June core PCE at +0.1% month-on-month and 3.3% year-on-year leans dovish, and the sharp early-August fall in crude and European gas materially improves the disinflation arithmetic Cook described as decisive. Worth noting that aluminium, copper and zinc all rose on 06-Aug DESPITE a firmer dollar - the base complex traded its own supply arithmetic. Decision point: the 15-16 September FOMC with dots.

THE RED SEA CONSTRAINT IS SEPARATE FROM HORMUZ AND IS NOT ADDRESSED BY THE ROUTING AGREEMENT, WHICH MATTERS SPECIFICALLY FOR EUROPEAN DELIVERED COSTS. The Bab al-Mandeb leg that carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam via Suez remains impaired independently of the Strait of Hormuz, so even a full Hormuz reopening would not restore the European delivered chain. Analysts have warned that disruption at both chokepoints simultaneously forces vessels to reroute via the Cape of Good Hope, lengthening transit times and raising freight and insurance costs. Adding to this independently of any geopolitics, the Baltic Dry Index rose 4.33% to 3,063 on 05-Aug, a fifth consecutive gain and +53.6% year-on-year, with part of the move attributed to Typhoon Dolphin. That is a freight cost increase a Hormuz reopening would not reverse, and it puts a floor under European delivered premiums the market may be discounting.

caveats: SOURCE AVAILABILITY, AND IT IS THE HEADLINE CAVEAT FOR THIS RUN. At this compile Westmetall had NOT published the 06-Aug LME board on either the English or the German overview, and BOTH per-metal daily tables still ended at 05-Aug - the first time the documented lag hit both language versions and both page types simultaneously. The 06-Aug session was nevertheless already inside Westmetall's own PUBLISHED August month-to-date averages pages, which had rolled from three sessions to four.

METHOD FOR THE 06-AUG BOARD, STATED IN FULL BECAUSE IT IS NOT THE NORMAL PATH. Every 06-Aug official on this board was RECOVERED ARITHMETICALLY from two published Westmetall figures - the August month-to-date mean and the 03/04/05-Aug daily table - rather than read directly. For each metal the back-solve resolves to a UNIQUE value inside LME's 0.50 tick (aluminium: 3,255.25 x 4 = 13,021.00 less 9,760.00 = 3,261.00 exactly), and each recovered stock figure lands on LME's 25 t reporting increment, 6 t for nickel. This is arithmetic on published data, not an estimate, but it is a departure from direct reading and is disclosed as such.

TWO INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECKS AGREE WITH THE RECOVERED BOARD. Westmetall's own 06-Aug German copper notations jumped about 2.0% on the day, consistent with the recovered copper cash of $14,455.00 (+2.03%). Trading Economics' separate 06-Aug marks on a different CFD basis - aluminium 3,261.95, zinc 3,793.35, lead 1,898.03, nickel 16,735.38 - match the recovered board in direction on every metal and in level to within a few dollars on aluminium.

SPREAD CONVENTION, STATED EVERY RUN: cash ABOVE 3M is BACKWARDATION; cash BELOW 3M is CONTANGO. The 06-Aug board shows cash $3,261.00 over 3M $3,260.00 - a $1.00 BACKWARDATION, replacing the $0.50 CONTANGO of 05-Aug. DIVERGENCE CALLED OUT EXPLICITLY: on 06-Aug the flat price rose $30.50 while the spread widened only $1.50, so price recovered far faster than structure. This is the mirror of 05-Aug, when spread and flat price fell together.

THE PHYSICAL PREMIUM COMPLEX IS THE WEAKEST-SOURCED BLOCK ON THIS BOARD AND THAT IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. Platts, Fastmarkets and Argus premium assessments are subscription products. A dedicated public search this run returned NO regional premium assessment dated in August 2026 for CIF Japan, EDU Rotterdam, Rotterdam billets, US Midwest transaction or US Midwest duty-paid; every one of those rows is carried at an assessment date of 03-Jul-2026 or earlier. The only current, independently verifiable premium figures here are the MJP Q3-2026 QUARTERLY SETTLEMENT of $395/t and the tariff decomposition.

THE Q4-2026 MJP FIGURE IS A SCENARIO RANGE, NOT AN ASSESSMENT. No public producer offers, negotiation levels or settlement coverage dated after 06-Jul-2026 could be found; talks are expected to open around late August. The range was narrowed to $320-415 this run and is a construct.

SECTION 232 VERIFIED AT 50% ON ALUMINIUM ARTICLES against CBP guidance CSMS #68855869 implementing Proclamation 11032, effective 08-Jun-2026.
